Readwise Keeper

Your forgotten highlights, back when you ask.

Try saying

What have I highlighted about focus?

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Readwise Keeper

Highlighting is the easy part. You read something good, you mark the paragraph, and then it goes into a library you will open once more, maybe, in two years.

The value was never in the marking. It is in the paragraph coming back at the moment you need it, and that only happens if something is watching for the moment.

Connect Readwise and your agent reads your real library. Ask what you have saved about a subject and it searches every book, article and podcast you have highlighted and answers with your own words, and where they came from. Ask what is in a particular book and it reads that book's highlights back. Ask for something you have forgotten and it pulls from the daily review.

It works best on the library you already have. Nothing to set up, nothing to tag.

Works with

  • Readwise

Setting up Readwise Keeper

  1. Get the token at readwise.io/access_token. It is one page with the token on it, and nothing else to set.

The Morning Show

Your daily briefing, delivered as a radio segment.

Run the evening wind-downTuesday, and it's done. FIRST UP: nothing tomorrow until eleven. The dentist is Thursday at 8:15, and that is the next early start. ON YOUR DESK: all four tasks closed. Nothing rolled into tomorrow. THE MONEY DESK: quiet today. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING: your mom's birthday is Saturday and nothing is bought yet. Three days is still plenty. That's the day. Back at seven.

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about The Morning Show

Archie sends things on their own schedule: a morning briefing, a market open, an evening wind-down, a weekly review. The Morning Show gives them a format. Every broadcast has a cold open, the same named segments in the same order (first up, on your desk, the money desk, one thing worth knowing), a one-clause handoff between them, and a one-line sign-off. The repetition is the value: after three days you know where your part lives and you can skim straight to it. An empty segment gets four words rather than padding, so the bit never makes a briefing longer than the plain facts would be. Mornings run up-tempo, evenings are slower and shorter. Reply to it and the show is over: it talks like a normal person until the next scheduled digest, then picks the format back up. Bad news is always read straight.

The Morning Show in a conversation

Run the morning showTuesday the fourth, and it fills right up after lunch. FIRST UP: standup at nine, thirty minutes. Nothing to prepare for it, and you are clear again until eleven. ON YOUR DESK: three meetings. Standup at nine, client review at eleven, Kessler at four. That last one is across town, so it wants half an hour of travel either side. Two tasks due, and the proposal is the one that actually matters. THE MONEY DESK: electric bill lands Thursday, 118 dollars. Nothing else moved. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING: the dishwasher part ships today, so somebody needs to be home Friday. That's the morning. Back at seven tomorrow.Can you drop the money desk? I don't want to hear it right now.Dropped. It stays out of the lineup until you say otherwise, and I have made a note of that. One thing I am not going to bury in a segment first: the car insurance is fourteen days past due and the policy ends on the 20th. That is the only item in there with a real deadline. Everything else was routine, and none of it is urgent. Do you want me to put the payment link in front of you once, tomorrow morning, and then leave it alone?Run the evening wind-downTuesday, and it's done. FIRST UP: nothing tomorrow until eleven.
